source_ref: ITEM TEXT, INSTRUCTIONS, ANCHORS: Singelis, T. M., distribution letter + form "Included below is the latest version of the Self-Construal Scale (SCS)", hosted by the Waterloo Wisdom and Culture Lab at https://uwaterloo.ca/wisdom-and-culture-lab/sites/default/files/uploads/files/singelis_update_singelis_2007_english.pdf (3 pp., sha256 d658059112ee32ec0ccd275a9f32877c5dd858463db94e463b038b08ea78b265, fetched 2026-09-10; text via pdftotext). RESPONSE DATA: OSF https://osf.io/wsjkb/ (no node licence field returned by the OSF API), files "SCS EA dataset.sav" (osf.io/download/5qz3w, 361 rows) and "SCS Korean dataset.sav" (osf.io/download/tfjx3, 320 rows); study syntax "SCS_CFA syntax.R" (osf.io/download/qx2r6). Processing script data/SCS_Suh_2023.r. PAPER: Suh, Jo, Turner, Antiporda & Ahn (2024), International Journal of Cognitive Therapy, doi:10.1007/s41811-024-00214-3 -- closed access (Unpaywall/OpenAlex oa_status=closed; Springer page returns a bot challenge), NOT read.
note: INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): the live table is 30 items SCS_1..SCS_30 on 1-7, 681 persons (320 Korea + 361 US, matching the paper abstract 320 Korean adults / 361 European Americans). This is Singelis’s 30-item Self-Construal Scale, as the dictionary Description says -- NOT Neff’s Self-Compassion Scale, which availability_audit_full.csv names for this table (that audit row is wrong: Neff’s SCS is 26 items on 1-5). CODE DERIVATION: data/SCS_Suh_2023.r pivots the .sav columns starting with SCS (SCS_short_1/2 excluded by case-insensitive starts_with) with names kept, so each item code IS a .sav column name -- no positional step. But the two .sav files carry NO variable labels and NO value labels on any column (checked with haven), so nothing in the deposit ties SCS_n to wording. The tie is the instrument’s own printed numbering 1-30 in Singelis’s letter; mapping_basis=paper_explicit in the moe2025_scs sense (instrument numbering against numbered codes), not a code list published by Suh et al. Supporting evidence that the study numbers items the Singelis way: its own SCS_CFA syntax.R Model3 ("2 factors based on Singles (30 item)") uses exactly the letter’s independent set {1,2,5,7,9,10,13,15,18,20,22,24,25,27,29}, and Model4 (24 item) drops exactly the letter’s six added items (5,7,24 and 12,14,30). VERIFICATION: route 5 PARTIAL -- see verify_SCS_Suh_2023_SCS.R (30/30 items closer to own subscale, permutation max 24/30; 8/9 content-twin pairs mutual top-3). LANGUAGE / FALLBACK: the Korean sample (320) will have been administered a Korean SCS (paper title: "...SCS-Short Version for Korean Adults"); the US sample (361) English. Neither .sav holds any text in any script and the paper and its supplements are closed access, so no Korean wording is recoverable within scope. Per the Step-4 fallback: Singelis’s English in the base fields, language=Korean, the four _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english. language=Korean is inferred from the sample, not stated in the deposit. For the US half the English IS the administered language, but whether Suh et al. used the letter’s wording verbatim (in particular its replacement item #2 rather than Singelis 1994’s original first-name item #2) could not be confirmed without the paper. OPTION TEXT: all seven anchors are printed in the letter (1=STRONGLY DISAGREE ... 4=DON’T AGREE OR DISAGREE ... 7=STRONGLY AGREE), transcribed with its casing and curly apostrophe. The study’s own anchors are unconfirmed; direction checked only by plausibility (SCS_1 "I enjoy being unique..." US mean 5.41 vs Korea 3.36, the largest group gap of the 30). Items stored raw; the SCS has no reverse-keyed items. DEVIATIONS: PDF line wraps collapsed to single spaces; the "____n." answer blanks and numbering stripped; the instrument field is IRW’s label, not a printed title. RIGHTS (ship-shaped -- ESCALATE, no register row written per the 2026-09-10 rule): the originator’s own letter, same PDF as above, states "Please feel free to use the SCS in your research. I ask only that you send me a copy of your findings for my archives. If you translate the scale please send me a copy and any equivalence or validity data you may provide." and later "It may be useful to contact me before the translation begins because I may be able to facilitate the process." Read as a research-use grant plus courtesy requests: no fee, no non-commercial/only clause, no permission-required route, no no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. Closest precedent is the ERQ page ("may be used for academic research purposes with appropriate citation"), ruled shippable 2026-09-08 (irw#2121). SPARQtools and stressmeasurement.org SCS pages state no terms. Different instrument from the blocked 32-item INDCOL (Singelis et al. 1995) in instrument_rights_register.csv -- that block does not reach this scale.
public_note: The Korean half of this sample (320 of 681) answered a Korean-language Self-Construal Scale whose wording is not in the deposit; the item text shipped is Singelis’s English form, the administered language for the 361 US respondents only.

source_ref: Ramsay J (2023) TestGardener R package, CRAN (GPL-3). WORDS+MAPPING: TestGardener_3.1.1.tar.gz from https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/TestGardener/ (sha256 0a313a2127b176435ed9c4a80c2012133c9b0efe8f601a326624fb07edfd42e7; the version data/TestGardener.R names), vignettes/SDS.Rmd itemVec (sha256 23bf2899329a3e1ddf3efae7d3a83cdf46a4300794cb61af80fc729917ca49c6) and data/SDS_U.rda (sha256 7f56828fe73dbc3b7d4f15eaac91bcc5f5d064d495db59b2cca793f31bdcb46d). CORROBORATION ONLY (no wording copied): Ramsay JO, Li J, Wiberg M, Better Test Scores with TestGardener (draft 2020-03-02), https://www.psych.mcgill.ca/misc/fda/downloads/FDAfuns/OptimalScoreBook.pdf (sha256 e272cf2a2ffb6d29700333c159f6de2d7423ab3c2d8be71085aca0e78c9a270d), sec. 2.10 numbered list and Fig. 5.8-5.10 captions. Processing script data/TestGardener.R. Cached under itemtext/.cache/sds/.
note: CODE DERIVATION: positional. data/TestGardener.R sets item=i over 1:ncol(SDS_U); verify_sds.R shows live item i equals SDS_U column i cell for cell (473 rows) and matches no other column, 13/13. WORDS+MAPPING: item_text is the SDS vignette's itemVec verbatim, which the vignette passes as optList$itemLab so column i is labelled itemVec[i]; the book (sec. 2.10) numbers the same 13 symptoms 1-13 in the same order with slightly longer wording (Bowel-related symptoms, Breathing-related symptoms, Intensity/Frequency of nausea distress, General outlook on life, Deterioration of appearance), hence mapping_basis=paper_explicit. The shipped SDS_dataList has optList$itemLab NULL and SDS_U has no dimnames, so there are no data-file labels (not data_labels). WHAT THE WORDS ARE: the package authors' descriptors of the 13 symptoms, NOT the questionnaire wording respondents read. The symptom set (nausea intensity+frequency, pain intensity+frequency, appetite, sleep, fatigue, bowel, concentration, appearance, outlook, breathing, cough) is that of McCorkle & Young (1978) Cancer Nursing 1(5):373-378, but neither the package nor the book names McCorkle, the administering study, or the form used, and the package's item order differs from the McCorkle form's, so the canonical statement-per-level form was NOT substituted (administered version unknown; the 1978 article is paywalled). instrument = 'Symptom Distress Scale' as the package names it. instructions/section_prompt blank: none published. OPTIONS: option_text blank for all 6 levels. The vignette's optVec labels options 1-5 only with the rating numbers '0'..'4' and option 6 with ' ' -- scores, not option wording, so not shipped as text. Per the vignette and SDS.Rd, resp 1-5 = ratings 0-4 in increasing intensity/frequency of distress (book sec. 5.4: first category = lowest intensity; resp 1 is the modal level on 12/13 items) and resp 6 is TestGardener's added 'sixth choice for missing or illegal responses'. RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT (reported, not fixed): the IRW table keeps resp=6 (missing/illegal sentinel) as a response value: 177 of 6149 rows, per item 4/10/4/3/3/3/9/79/9/43/1/5/4; it is not a higher distress level. Item 8 (Frequency of nausea) has 79 sixes, all where item 7 = 1 (75) or item 7 = 6 (4) -- a skip, not an answer; item 10 has 43 (35 where item 9 = 1). RIGHTS: text copied from the GPL-3 package vignette. No restriction on the McCorkle SDS wording was found, and its statements are not shipped; no register row exists or was written. The book PDF front matter reads 'This version is temporary because it is still evolving, and must not be distributed' -- a bar on redistributing the draft book, from which nothing was copied (used only to corroborate numbering and Fig. 5.9).
public_note: Item text for this table is the TestGardener package authors' short labels for the 13 symptoms, not the questionnaire wording; response options are unlabelled in the source -- resp 1-5 are distress ratings 0-4 in increasing order, and resp 6 is the package's code for a missing or illegal response rather than a sixth rating level

source_ref: PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0240103 (Shan, Hussain & Sargani 2020, CC BY 4.0), S1 File (.s001, SPSS .sav): variable labels of G1/G2 and their value labels 1-5; cross-checked against the article's 'On guilt' discussion paragraph (Item 25 mean 2.54, Item 26 mean 2.36) and data/shan_2020_acculturative_stress.py
note: item codes G1/G2 ARE the .sav column names (data/shan_2020_acculturative_stress.py melts SCALES['shan_2020_g']=['G1','G2'] unrenamed), so there is no positional step. item_text is each column's SPSS variable label verbatim ('I feel guilty to leave my family and friends behind.' / 'I feel guilty that I am living a different life style here.'), including the study's 'life style' spelling; names and labels agree (both Guilt items sit under the G prefix, and the .sav's own Guilt column equals G1+G2 for all 203 rows). option_text is the .sav value labels verbatim, lowercase as stored (1 strongly disagree .. 5 strongly agree); the script reads labels via pd.read_spss and maps them back through LIKERT_MAP to the same integers. Checked, not assumed: live per-item x level counts equal the .sav's cell for cell, 10/10 (G1 46/65/47/25/20, G2 50/79/40/18/16), and source means 2.5468/2.3645 match the paper's Item 25 'I feel guilty leaving my friends and family behind' 2.54 and Item 26 2.36 (paper paraphrases item 25 slightly; the .sav label was shipped). instructions left blank: the paper only describes the format ('Each item was answered on 5 Point Likert Scale, as 1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree'), no respondent-facing instruction text is published. Language: survey administration language not stated (interviews were in Urdu); the only questionnaire wording in the deposit or paper is English, so shipped as English with no language/_translated columns. Rights: ASSIS originates with Sandhu & Asrabadi (1994) Psychological Reports 75(1):435-48; searched the SAGE record and web for a use/permission/redistribution clause on 2026-09-10 and found none to quote, so silence applies; wording shipped is the study's own CC BY labels. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). S1 .sav sha256 f0f1b8474dc92123476651e36bf43cbeac80f400bb70a66c3d813c39c57dee7c. Response-data observation (not a text defect): ID 178 appears on two .sav rows with different Gender, so the live table has 202 unique ids over 203 respondents per item.

source_ref: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0240103 (Shan et al. 2020, PLOS ONE, CC BY 4.0): S1 File pone.0240103.s001 (.sav) variable labels HS1-HS4 and value labels; article Table 7 (item wording with per-item M/SD)
note: mapping_basis=data_labels: data/shan_2020_acculturative_stress.py takes item codes straight from the .sav column names HS1..HS4 (no rename, no positional assignment), and the .sav's own VARIABLE labels give the wording for all 4/4 (the script's header comment 'no item text in the file' is wrong -- pd.read_spss discards labels; pyreadstat shows them). Wording: HS1-HS3 verbatim from the .sav variable labels, identical to Table 7 of the article; HS4 taken from Table 7 ('...country of my origin.') because the .sav label reads 'origion' -- a one-character typo correction from the study's own paper, disclosed here. option_text = the .sav VALUE labels verbatim (lowercase: 1 'strongly disagree' .. 5 'strongly agree'), matching the script's LIKERT_MAP and the paper ('1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree'). Cross-checks run anyway (not required for data_labels): live per-item means 3.6207/3.3103/2.8621/3.7537 equal Table 7's published 3.6207/3.3103/2.8621/3.7537 exactly and equal the .sav means; live per-item response counts equal .sav value counts cell for cell (HS1 16/17/48/69/53, HS2 18/38/50/57/40, HS3 32/55/46/49/21, HS4 10/15/46/76/56), so option_text<->resp is also confirmed (route 9). Subscale identity: the paper states Homesickness = items 9-12, which are the HS1-HS4 columns in Table 7 order. Instructions left blank: the paper and supplements (S2/S3 are only reviewer-response letters) print no respondent instructions. Language: treated as an English administration -- the .sav labels and Table 7 are English, the paper names Urdu only as the interview language and mentions no translation of the survey; not explicitly stated. Rights: ASSIS (Sandhu & Asrabadi 1994, Psychological Reports 75:435-448); no instrument_rights_register row; no rights-holder statement reserving any right was located (two web searches; SAGE article page only). availability_audit_full.csv calls the ASSIS '(non-commercial)' but cites no clause, and none was found -- silence is permission, so not a block; no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). Response-data defect (does not affect item text): source .sav has ID 178 on two different respondents (rows 168 and 178; one Male, one Female), so the live table has 202 unique ids, 812 rows, and two rows per item for id 178 -- a dup_id_item defect shared by every shan_2020_* sibling.
